Main article: [Economy of the European Union](/wiki/Economy_of_the_European_Union "Economy of the European Union")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Europe-GDP-PPP-per-capita-map.png/250px-Europe-GDP-PPP-per-capita-map.png)](/wiki/File:Europe-GDP-PPP-per-capita-map.png)

[GDP](/wiki/GDP "GDP") (PPP) per capita (including non-EU countries)

The [gross domestic product](/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") (GDP), a measure of economic activity, of EU member states was US$16.64 trillion in 2022, around 16.6 per cent of the world GDP.[[180]](#cite_note-199) There is a significant variation in GDP per capita between and within individual EU states. The difference between the richest and poorest regions (281 NUTS-2 regions of the [Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics](/wiki/Nomenclature_of_Territorial_Units_for_Statistics "Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics")) ranged, in 2017, from 31 per cent (Severozapaden, Bulgaria) of the EU28 average (€30,000) to 253 per cent (Luxembourg), or from €4,600 to €92,600.[[181]](#cite_note-200)

EU member states own the estimated third largest after the United States (US$140 trillion) and [China](/wiki/China "China") (US$84 trillion) [net wealth](/wiki/Net_wealth "Net wealth") in the world, equal to around one sixth (US$76 trillion) of the US$454 trillion global wealth.[[182]](#cite_note-databook2023-201) Of the top [500 largest corporations in the world measured by revenue](/wiki/Fortune_Global_500 "Fortune Global 500") in 2024, 90 had their headquarters in the EU.[[183]](#cite_note-202) In 2016, unemployment in the EU stood at 8.9 per cent[[184]](#cite_note-UNEMP-203) while inflation was at 2.2 per cent, and the account balance at −0.9 per cent of GDP. The average annual net earnings in the European Union was around €25,000[[185]](#cite_note-204) in 2021.

[Amancio Ortega](/wiki/Amancio_Ortega "Amancio Ortega") rose from last year's position of number four to second.[[23]](#cite_note-forbes-23) [Warren Buffett](/wiki/Warren_Buffett "Warren Buffett") of [Berkshire Hathaway](/wiki/Berkshire_Hathaway "Berkshire Hathaway") came in third for the second consecutive time,[[24]](#cite_note-24) while Mexican telecommunication mogul [Carlos Slim](/wiki/Carlos_Slim "Carlos Slim") slipped from last year's second position to fourth. [Jeff Bezos](/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos") of [Amazon](/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"),[[25]](#cite_note-forbes.com-25) [Mark Zuckerberg](/wiki/Mark_Zuckerberg "Mark Zuckerberg") of [Facebook](/wiki/Facebook "Facebook")[[26]](#cite_note-26) and [Michael Bloomberg](/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg") of [Bloomberg L.P.](/wiki/Bloomberg_L.P. "Bloomberg L.P."),[[27]](#cite_note-27) appeared for the first time on the *Forbes* top 10 billionaires list, coming at fifth, sixth and eighth positions, respectively. Zuckerberg became the youngest top 10 billionaire this year at the age of 31. [Larry Ellison](/wiki/Larry_Ellison "Larry Ellison"), [Charles Koch](/wiki/Charles_Koch "Charles Koch") and [David Koch](/wiki/David_Koch "David Koch") also slipped from their previous year's positions, with Ellison dropping to seventh from fifth, and the Kochs falling to ninth position from sixth.

*Variety* opined that Johansson's roles in *Lost in Translation* and *Girl with a Pearl Earring* established her as among the most versatile actresses of her generation.[[25]](#cite_note-variety-25) Johansson had five releases in 2004, three of which—the teen heist film *[The Perfect Score](/wiki/The_Perfect_Score "The Perfect Score")*, the drama *[A Love Song for Bobby Long](/wiki/A_Love_Song_for_Bobby_Long "A Love Song for Bobby Long")*, and the drama *[A Good Woman](/wiki/A_Good_Woman_(film) "A Good Woman (film)")*—were critical and commercial failures.[[53]](#cite_note-BOM-54) Co-starring with [John Travolta](/wiki/John_Travolta "John Travolta"), Johansson played a discontented teenager in *A Love Song for Bobby Long*, which is based on the novel *Off Magazine Street* by Ronald Everett Capps. David Rooney of *Variety* wrote that Johansson's and Travolta's performances rescued the film.[[54]](#cite_note-55) Johansson earned a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Drama](/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama") nomination for the film.[[51]](#cite_note-GGlobe-51)

Harbin Institute of Technology [Shenzhen](/wiki/Shenzhen "Shenzhen") campus

Its faculty and students have invented many 'firsts' in China: the first [analog computer](/wiki/Analog_computer "Analog computer") in 1957, the first digital computer in 1958, the first intelligent [chess computer](/wiki/Chess_computer "Chess computer"), the first arc welding [robot](/wiki/Robot "Robot"), the first world-class new system [radar](/wiki/Radar "Radar"), the first [IC](/wiki/Integrated_circuit "Integrated circuit") [CMOS](/wiki/CMOS "CMOS") chip with its own copyright, the first superway, computer real-time [3D image](/wiki/3D_image "3D image") creation system, and the first high-performance computer controlled [fiber twister](/wiki/Fiber "Fiber").[[39]](#cite_note-39)[[40]](#cite_note-40) HIT undertakes research covered by [official secrets](/wiki/Classified_information "Classified information") (e.g. in [space science](/wiki/Space_science "Space science") and [defense](/wiki/Defense_(military) "Defense (military)")-related technologies).[[41]](#cite_note-41)[[42]](#cite_note-42) It made the largest contribution to the success of the [Shenzhou series spacecraft](/wiki/Shenzhou_spacecraft "Shenzhou spacecraft") and [Kuaizhou](/wiki/Kuaizhou "Kuaizhou") series spacecraft.[[43]](#cite_note-43)[[44]](#cite_note-44) One minor planet (#55838) is named after the Harbin Institute of Technology and nicknamed "Hagongda Star" by the [International Astronomical Union](/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") for HIT's achievements in science and engineering.[[45]](#cite_note-45)[[46]](#cite_note-46)

fanoutqa_028577.x:
Western Front (World War II) :: 1939–1940: Axis victories :: Operation Weserübung :: chunk_0005
While the Western Front remained quiet in April 1940, the fighting between the Allies and the Germans began in earnest with the [Norwegian Campaign](/wiki/Norwegian_Campaign "Norwegian Campaign") when the Germans launched [Operation Weserübung](/wiki/Operation_Weser%C3%BCbung "Operation Weserübung"), the German invasion of Denmark and Norway. In doing so, the Germans beat the Allies to the punch; the Allies had been planning an amphibious landing in which they could begin to surround Germany, cutting off her supply of raw materials from [Sweden](/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"). However, when the Allies made a counter-landing in Norway following the German invasion, the Germans repulsed them and defeated the Norwegian armed forces, driving the latter [into exile](/wiki/Norwegian_Armed_Forces_in_exile "Norwegian Armed Forces in exile"). The *[Kriegsmarine](/wiki/Kriegsmarine "Kriegsmarine")*, nonetheless, suffered very heavy losses during the two months of fighting required to seize all of mainland Norway.

The **Netherlands national football team** ([Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language"): *Nederlands voetbalelftal* or simply *Het Nederlands elftal*) has represented the [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in international men's [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") matches since 1905. The men's national team is controlled by the [Royal Dutch Football Association](/wiki/Royal_Dutch_Football_Association "Royal Dutch Football Association") (KNVB), the governing body for [football in the Netherlands](/wiki/Football_in_the_Netherlands "Football in the Netherlands"), which is a part of [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"), under the jurisdiction of [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA "FIFA"). Most of the Netherlands home matches are played at the [Johan Cruyff Arena](/wiki/Johan_Cruyff_Arena "Johan Cruyff Arena"), [De Kuip](/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip"), [Philips Stadion](/wiki/Philips_Stadion "Philips Stadion") and [De Grolsch Veste](/wiki/De_Grolsch_Veste "De Grolsch Veste").

Pink represents the Women in the United States Senate

There are 26 women currently serving in the United States Senate. This is the highest number of women to have served concurrently in U.S. Senate history. Sixteen are Democrats and ten are Republicans.

The record was first achieved in January 2020 when [Kelly Loeffler](/wiki/Kelly_Loeffler "Kelly Loeffler") was appointed to the Senate from Georgia, increasing the number of women in the Senate from 25 to 26. The number fell back to 25 on December 2 of the same year when [Martha McSally](/wiki/Martha_McSally "Martha McSally")'s appointment ended after she lost an election to finish [John McCain](/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain")'s unexpired term. The record of 26 was reached again on January 3, 2021, when [Cynthia Lummis](/wiki/Cynthia_Lummis "Cynthia Lummis"), the first female senator from Wyoming, began her term. The record was sustained for only 15 days, as the number of concurrently serving women dropped again to 25 when [Kamala Harris](/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") resigned her Senate seat on January 18 in anticipation of the scheduled commencement of her term as vice president (and thus president of the Senate) on January 20.

A [Saturn V](/wiki/Saturn_V "Saturn V") rocket launched Apollo 11 from [Launch Complex 39A](/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Launch_Complex_39A "Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A") at the [Kennedy Space Center](/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") on July 16, 1969, at 13:32:00 [UTC](/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") (09:32:00 EDT local time).[[118]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOrloff200092-118) Armstrong's wife Janet and two sons watched from a yacht moored on the [Banana River](/wiki/Banana_River "Banana River").[[119]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen20052-119) During the launch, Armstrong's heart rate peaked at 110 beats per minute.[[120]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005410-120) He found the first stage the loudest, much noisier than the Gemini 8 Titan II launch. The Apollo command module was relatively roomy compared with the Gemini spacecraft. None of the Apollo 11 crew suffered [space sickness](/wiki/Space_sickness "Space sickness"), as some members of previous crews had. Armstrong was especially glad about this, as he had been prone to [motion sickness](/wiki/Motion_sickness "Motion sickness") as a child and could experience [nausea](/wiki/Nausea "Nausea") after long periods of [aerobatics](/wiki/Aerobatics "Aerobatics").[[121]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen2005411–412-121)

The municipality of [Chongqing](/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing"), China, whose administrative jurisdictional area is approximately the size of [Austria](/wiki/Austria "Austria"), has the largest population of any [city proper](/wiki/City_proper "City proper"); over 70% of its residents live in [rural areas](/wiki/Rural_area "Rural area").

A city can be defined by its administrative boundaries, otherwise known as [city proper](/wiki/City_proper "City proper"). [UNICEF](/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") defines city proper as, "the population living within the administrative boundaries of a city or controlled directly from the city by a single authority." A city proper is a locality defined according to legal or political boundaries and an administratively recognised urban status that is usually characterised by some form of [local government](/wiki/Local_government "Local government").[[1]](#cite_note-wup2007-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) Cities proper and their boundaries and population data may not include suburbs.[[4]](#cite_note-wup2003-4)

The use of city proper as defined by administrative boundaries may not include suburban areas where an important proportion of the population working or studying in the city lives.[[4]](#cite_note-wup2003-4) Because of this definition, the city proper population figure may differ greatly from the urban area population figure, as many cities are amalgamations of smaller municipalities, and conversely, many Chinese cities govern territories that extend well beyond the core urban area into suburb

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Hydrogen_production_via_Electrolysis.png/250px-Hydrogen_production_via_Electrolysis.png)](/wiki/File:Hydrogen_production_via_Electrolysis.png)

Inputs and outputs of the electrolysis of water production of hydrogen

[Electrolysis of water](/wiki/Electrolysis_of_water "Electrolysis of water") is a conceptually simple method of producing hydrogen.

2 H2O(l) → 2 H2(g) + O2(g)

Commercial [electrolyzers](/wiki/Electrolyzer "Electrolyzer") use [nickel](/wiki/Nickel "Nickel")-based catalysts in strongly alkaline solution. [Platinum](/wiki/Platinum "Platinum") is a better catalyst but is expensive.[[122]](#cite_note-122) The hydrogen created through electrolysis using renewable energy is commonly referred to as "[green hydrogen](/wiki/Green_hydrogen "Green hydrogen")".[[123]](#cite_note-RoyalSociety-2021-123)

[Electrolysis](/wiki/Electrolysis "Electrolysis") of [brine](/wiki/Brine "Brine") to yield [chlorine](/wiki/Chlorine "Chlorine")[[124]](#cite_note-124) also produces high-purity hydrogen as a co-product, which is used for a variety of transformations such as [hydrogenations](/wiki/Hydrogenation "Hydrogenation").[[125]](#cite_note-125)

The electrolysis process is more expensive than producing hydrogen from methane without [carbon capture and storage](/wiki/Carbon_capture_and_storage "Carbon capture and storage").[[126]](#cite_note-Evans-2020-126)

Innovation in [hydrogen electrolyzers](/wiki/Hydrogen_electrolyzer "Hydrogen electrolyzer") could make large-scale production of hydrogen from electricity more cost-competitive.[[127]](#cite_note-127)

The kennel clubs which do not recognise the Medium Poodle variety typically have the Standard Poodle between 38 and 60 centimetres (15 and 24 in) and Miniature Poodle between 28 and 38 centimetres (11 and 15 in), with the toy variety remaining unchanged.[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5)

A healthy adult Standard Poodle typically weighs between 20 and 32 kilograms (44 and 71 lb), a Medium Poodle between 15 and 19 kilograms (33 and 42 lb), a Miniature Poodle between 12 and 14 kilograms (26 and 31 lb) and a Toy Poodle between 6.5 and 7.5 kilograms (14 and 17 lb).[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)

View of Tokyo from the top of the [Tokyo Skytree](/wiki/Tokyo_Skytree "Tokyo Skytree"). The [Greater Tokyo Area](/wiki/Greater_Tokyo_Area "Greater Tokyo Area") is ranked as the [most populous metropolitan area](/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_by_population "List of metropolitan areas by population") in the world.

Japan has a population of nearly 123 million, of whom almost 119 million are Japanese nationals; foreign residents make up the remainder, estimated at 3,743,000 as of September 2025.[[234]](#cite_note-235) Japan is one of the world's [fastest aging countries](/wiki/Aging_of_Japan "Aging of Japan") and has the highest proportion of [elderly citizens](/wiki/Elderly_people_in_Japan "Elderly people in Japan") of any country, comprising [one-third of its total population](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_age_structure "List of countries by age structure");[[235]](#cite_note-EUAgeing-236) this is the result of a [post–World War II baby boom](/wiki/Post%E2%80%93World_War_II_baby_boom "Post–World War II baby boom"), which was followed by an increase in life expectancy and a decrease in [birth rates](/wiki/Birth_rate "Birth rate").[[236]](#cite_note-237)

fanoutqa_011425.x:
Gansu :: Economy :: chunk_0013
Despite recent growth in Gansu and the booming economy in the rest of China, Gansu is still considered to be one of the poorest provinces in China. For several years, it has [ranked as one of the provinces with lowest GDP per capita](/wiki/List_of_Chinese_provincial-level_divisions_by_GDP_per_capita "List of Chinese provincial-level divisions by GDP per capita").[[33]](#cite_note-:0-37) Its nominal GDP for 2017 was about 767.7 billion yuan (US$113.70 billion) and per capita of 29,326 RMB (US$4,343). The province also has a large difference in wealth between regions and urban versus rural areas. The poorest areas are Dingxi, Longnan, Gannan and Linxia.[[34]](#cite_note-:1-38) According to analysts, the local economy failed to gather momentum while other provinces did manage to increase their economic growth.[[33]](#cite_note-:0-37)
